evidence.title: Reviewed Cross-App and Excel Agent workflows need declarative E2E coverage
evidence.summary: Synthetic reviewed evidence used to exercise one production 1JS declarative E2E authoring batch across both supported owning workspaces without claiming a live incident.

requiredContracts: Create and preview a real workbook with a worksheet named Canary and a four-row by three-column table including one header row.
In the Omni AAD Excel Agent experience, write and verify an exact four-row by three-column grid in cells A1:C4.

review.observedBehavior: The controller has a Cross-App authoring fixture but no reviewed fixture proving that one batch can also route an Excel Agent case to its separate owning workspace and execution cohort.
review.expectedBehavior: One repository-native authoring batch should add independent Cross-App and Omni AAD Excel Agent declarations, preserve their separate local and CI evidence, and deliver them on one branch and Draft PR.
hypotheses: The existing BizChat setup, workbook creation composite and protected workbook verifier can express the Cross-App case without a new harness capability.
The existing Excel Agent prompt-turn, workbook-clear and exact-cell assertion contracts can express a deterministic A1:C4 grid without new provider behavior.
counterEvidence: The existing Cross-App six-by-five scenario covers a different worksheet and table contract and must not be renamed or weakened.
Existing Excel Agent write-string and write-workbook cases verify only one cell and do not cover the requested multi-cell grid contract.
review.rationale: The handoff requests source-bound coverage for two established workbook capabilities using the qualified repository-native authoring skill and its documented multi-workspace batch contract.
review.nextAction: Use the configured 1JS declarative E2E authoring skill. Preserve existing cases and add one distinct Cross-App AAD scenario plus one distinct Omni AAD Excel Agent scenario only where exact coverage is absent.

improvement.theme: Cross-App and Excel Agent declarative authoring batch coverage
improvement.rationale: Prove that reviewed evidence can route independent cases into both supported 1JS declarative E2E owning workspaces while retaining one authoring delivery.

coverageGaps: No dedicated AAD BizChat scenario verifies a Canary worksheet with a four-row by three-column Excel Table including one header row.
No dedicated Omni AAD Excel Agent scenario verifies a deterministic four-row by three-column grid written into A1:C4.
testCoverage.rationale: The qualified skill must inspect the exact 1JS revision, classify each item by starting surface, reuse current declarations and keep Cross-App and Excel Agent execution evidence attributable.

items.title: Create a Canary Excel workbook from BizChat
preconditions: The user is signed in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with the qualified AAD profile.
Record the current Try Fluxv4 value and Sydney variants so both can be restored.
orderedTestSteps: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat using the entry URL.
Turn off Try Fluxv4 if it is enabled.
Append the existing Office Agent MCP Sydney variants used by the current BizChat workbook scenario without removing existing variants.
Send the exact prompt: Create an Excel workbook with sheet 'Canary' and that contains a 4x3 table (contains header)
Wait for the response to complete.
Open the generated Excel workbook in the Excel preview panel.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: The response produces a real Excel .xlsx workbook.
The workbook opens in an Excel preview panel.
The workbook contains a worksheet named Canary.
The worksheet contains an Excel Table spanning exactly four total rows and three columns.
The first table row is the header row and the remaining three rows are table body rows; body cells may be empty.
cleanup: Restore the original Try Fluxv4 value.
Close only the tab created for this test.

items.title: Excel Agent writes a four-by-three grid in Omni
preconditions: The user is signed in with the qualified AAD enterprise profile.
The local or CloudTest launcher has selected the Omni Excel Agent experience.
Launch the existing AAD hub-create flow with a disposable blank workbook owned by this test.

The external owning registration workflow reserves semantic ID excel-agent.aad.write-four-by-three-grid, title Enterprise Excel Agent writes a four-by-three workbook grid, command e2e:ci:excel-agent:aad:write-four-by-three-grid, catalog number 33, tags omni-supported, arcadia-ongoing and omni-observing, and a capability-matrix row matching the authored declaration.
orderedTestSteps: Open the test-owned disposable blank workbook in Excel Online.
Open the Excel Copilot task pane and verify that the current experience is Omni.
Send the exact prompt: Fill cells A1:C4 with this exact grid. Row 1: Item, Quantity, Region. Row 2: Widget A, 2, West. Row 3: Widget B, 4, East. Row 4: Widget C, 6, Central.
Wait for the edit operation to complete.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: Excel Agent completes the workbook edit without switching away from Omni.
A1, B1 and C1 contain Item, Quantity and Region.
A2, B2 and C2 contain Widget A, 2 and West.
A3, B3 and C3 contain Widget B, 4 and East.
A4, B4 and C4 contain Widget C, 6 and Central.
cleanup: Keep the edited A1:C4 cells as result evidence because the AAD hub-created workbook is disposable.
Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test.
